 Log in Offseason approach, Whitlock, pitching depth among hot Reddit AMA topics
 November 6th, 2026 Ian Browne
 Share share-square--:R1qlq: This story was excerpted from Ian Browne’s Red Sox Beat newsletter. To read the full newsletter, click here . And subscribe to get it regularly in your inbox. 
 BOSTON -- Earlier this week, I held an Ask Me Anything on Reddit with Red Sox fans at r/redsox. This mailbag features questions and answers from there.
 The full AMA can be read if you click here .
 Questions and responses have been lightly edited for clarity. 
 What do you think is the more likely big-move scenario for the Red Sox this offseason? The farm system is in pretty good shape, but it's nowhere near as stocked as it was a year ago. Was the postseason loss enough to get the front office to consider emptying it out for a true impact bat via trade? Or does Craig Breslow just add another impact starting pitcher via free agency, like a Michael King or Freddy Peralta, to replace Sonny Gray? 
 Breslow has gone down the trade road a lot in his three previous offseasons as chief baseball officer. With the prospect haul that was sent to the Orioles for Adley Rutschman , this could be the year free agency is the option Breslow explores the most. Randy Arozarena, to me, would be the perfect fit in the middle of the batting order. I'm not sure how much they will invest in pitching considering that Garrett Crochet should be fully healthy. The front three in the rotation (Crochet, Payton Tolle and Ranger Suarez) seem pretty formidable. They also have Jake Bennett, who was solid last year as a rookie, and Tanner Houck, who is back from Tommy John surgery.

 Does the team view Garrett Whitlock as the heir to the closer? 
 I believe Whitlock is more of a setup man. He is excellent in that role and sometimes you shouldn't mess with what works. I'm guessing the Sox will again pick up Whitlock's option for 2028, like they did for next season. After '28, he will be a free agent, giving him a choice to pursue a closer's role either with Boston, someone else or even try to convert back to his old role of starting somewhere.
 What do you think about the bullpen?  
 The bullpen has as good a 1-2 punch as you can have with Whitlock in the eighth and Aroldis Chapman in the ninth. One underrated thing that really crushed the Red Sox going into the playoffs was the injury to Tyron Guerrero, not to mention Justin Slaten going down a few weeks before that. I think that each year in the playoffs, the teams that go deep into October have one strong bullpen option after another they throw at you from about the fifth through ninth innings. The Red Sox already have the makings of a strong bullpen, but they should continue to keep adding to it whenever possible.
 No one is talking back-end starters or bullpen arms. I think these are important for depth. Who are likely targets? 
 Even if the rotation looks to be a strong suit, you can never count out Breslow from adding more rotation depth, particularly if Gray signs elsewhere. One name that intrigues me? Shota Imanaga. Breslow was really fond of him when he was scouting him for the Cubs three years ago. The Cubs wound up signing him, but Breslow was in his early stages with the Red Sox at that point. On the international front, keep an eye on Kaima Taira, the righty who was recently posted by the Saitama Seibu Lions . Taira is known for his fastball, and has plenty of experience as both a starter and reliever.
 There seem to be a lot of backup catcher options on the market this offseason -- do you think there is any consideration of an upgrade from Connor Wong? He just had his second year in a row with negative fWAR (although bWAR tells a slightly different story).  
 Given that Wong is arbitration-eligible, the Red Sox have until Nov. 20 -- the non-tender deadline -- to make a decision on him. I do think this is probably the right time to evaluate whether he is still the best fit. Austin Hedges, Kyle Higashioka, James McCann, Gary Sánchez and Jake Rogers are some of the free agents on the market. Sánchez would certainly offer some right-handed power off the bench. Rogers was really comfortable in the very short stint he had with the Red Sox in August, and the pitchers all seemed to like him, so you wonder if they would re-explore that.
